s: Where is the Central Potato Research Institute located?
x: CPRI is at Shimla; CAZRI is at Jodhpur and NDRI at Karnal.

s: Where is the Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute located?
x: IGFRI is at Jhansi; Bhopal has the soil science institute and Karnal the NDRI.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA) is located at Hyderabad. The NRC on Camel is at Bikaner, NRC on Seed Spices at Ajmer and NRCWA at Bhubaneswar.

s: Where is the ICAR Central Soil Salinity Research Institute located?
x: CSSRI is at Karnal; Bhopal has the soil science institute (IISS).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Institute of Abiotic Stress Management – Raipur
National Institute of Abiotic Stress Management – Ranchi
National Institute of Biotic Stress Management – Malegaon
National Institute of Biotic Stress Management – Raipur
x: The National Institute of Biotic Stress Management is at Raipur; the National Institute of Abiotic Stress Management is at Malegaon near Baramati, Maharashtra.

s: Where is the Central Citrus Research Institute located?
x: The Central Citrus Research Institute is at Nagpur.

s: Where is the ICAR Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture located?
x: It is at Lucknow; Jhansi has the Agroforestry institute.

s: Where is the National Plant Protection Training Institute located?
x: NPPTI is in Hyderabad; the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage is at Faridabad.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: CIFA, the Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture, is located at Bhubaneswar, not Lucknow. NDRI, IIHR and CIAH are correctly matched.

s: Where is the Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) located?
x: CAZRI is at Jodhpur (1959); CIAH and NRC Camel are at Bikaner.

s: Where is the ICAR National Research Centre on Seed Spices located?
x: NRC Seed Spices is at Ajmer; Unjha is a seed-spice trading hub.

s: Which of the following ICAR institutes is correctly matched with its location?
x: NRRI is at Cuttack; CRIDA is at Hyderabad, CPRI at Shimla and NDRI at Karnal.

s: Where is the Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) located?
x: CIFA is at Bhubaneswar; CRRI/NRRI is at Cuttack and ICRISAT at Patancheru.

s: In which year was the Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur, established?
x: CAZRI, Jodhpur was set up in 1959.

s: In which year was the Central Tobacco Research Institute at Rajahmundry established?
x: CTRI, Rajahmundry (Andhra Pradesh) was set up in 1947.

s: Where is the ICAR National Research Centre on Camel located?
x: NRC on Camel (1984) is at Bikaner; CAZRI is at Jodhpur and NRC Seed Spices at Ajmer.

s: Where is the Central Tuber Crops Research Institute located?
x: The Central Tuber Crops Research Institute is at Thiruvananthapuram; CPCRI is at Kasaragod.

s: Which place is Asia's largest seed-spice trading hub?
x: Unjha in Mehsana, Gujarat is Asia's largest seed-spice trading hub; the NRC on Seed Spices is at Ajmer.

s: Where was the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) first set up in 1905?
x: IARI began at Pusa, Bihar in 1905 and moved to New Delhi in 1936.

s: Where is the International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) located?
x: ICRISAT, an international institute, is at Patancheru near Hyderabad.

s: Where was the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) first set up in 1923?
x: NDRI began at Bengaluru in 1923 and moved to Karnal in 1955.

s: In which year was the Central Rice Research Institute (now NRRI) at Cuttack set up?
x: CRRI, Cuttack, was set up in 1946; CPRI, Shimla, followed in 1949.

s: Which is the Indian lead institution for the Square Kilometre Array project?
x: NCRA-TIFR, Pune is the Indian lead institution for the Square Kilometre Array, whose facilities are located in South Africa and Australia.

s: Where is the FAIR accelerator located?
x: FAIR is at Darmstadt, Germany; Cadarache, France is the ITER site.

s: Which is the Indian lead institution for ITER?
x: ITER (Cadarache, France) has ITER-India at IPR Gandhinagar as the Indian lead institution.

s: LIGO-India is planned at Aundh in which district of Maharashtra?
x: LIGO-India's site is at Aundh, Hingoli district, with DAE, DST and the US NSF.

s: The MACE telescope is notable as which of the following?
x: MACE at Hanle, Ladakh, is described as the highest imaging Cherenkov telescope and is associated with BARC.

s: In what ratio do DST and DAE share India's participation in the FAIR accelerator?
x: For FAIR (Darmstadt), Bose Institute is the nodal institution and DST and DAE participate 50:50.

s: The India-based Neutrino Observatory (INO) is planned in which district of Tamil Nadu?
x: INO is at Bodi West Hills, Theni, with TIFR as host.

s: Which Indian institution leads both LIGO-India and ITER-India?
x: IPR Gandhinagar leads both; NCRA-TIFR leads the Square Kilometre Array.

s: Where is the Thirty Meter Telescope, in which India participates through DST and DAE, sited?
x: TMT is at Mauna Kea, Hawaii; IIA Bengaluru is involved.

s: LIGO-India is being built by DAE and DST in collaboration with which US agency?
x: LIGO-India at Aundh, Hingoli is a DAE-DST project with the US National Science Foundation.

s: Which institution built the MACE telescope at Hanle, Ladakh?
x: MACE, the highest imaging Cherenkov telescope, was built by BARC with ECIL and opened on 4 October 2024.

s: Which institute operates the 104-cm Sampurnanand Telescope?
x: The 104-cm Sampurnanand Telescope (1972) belongs to ARIES, Nainital.

s: Which institute built the VELC payload of Aditya-L1?
x: The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) of Aditya-L1 was built by IIA Bengaluru.

s: When were gravitational waves first directly detected?
x: LIGO first detected gravitational waves on 14 September 2015; the result was announced on 11 February 2016.

s: Who shared the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics for the detection of gravitational waves?
o: Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish and Kip Thorne
Roger Penrose, Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez
Arthur Ashkin, Gerard Mourou and Donna Strickland
x: The 2017 physics Nobel went to Weiss, Barish and Thorne for LIGO's detection of gravitational waves.

s: In which year was the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) established?
x: ICAR was established in 1929; DARE, its administrative department, came in December 1973.

s: ICAR functions under which department of the Ministry of Agriculture?
x: ICAR is under DARE (Dec 1973), Ministry of Agriculture.

s: Under which Act is the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) registered as a society?
x: ICAR is a registered society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860; it is not a statutory body.

s: In which year was the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) set up?
x: DARE was set up in December 1973 in the Ministry of Agriculture; ICAR functions under it.

s: Krishi Vigyan Kendras, 100% centrally funded under ICAR, function under how many ATARIs?
x: KVKs are district-level centres under ICAR, each under one of 11 ATARIs.

s: Where was the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra set up in 1974?
x: The first KVK was a pilot at Puducherry in 1974, under TNAU.

s: Against which disease is Lumpi-ProVacInd, developed by two ICAR institutes, used?
o: Foot and mouth disease in cattle
x: Lumpi-ProVacInd is an indigenous vaccine made by two ICAR institutes against lumpy skin disease in cattle.

s: On whose report was ICAR set up in 1929?
x: ICAR was set up on 16 July 1929 on the report of the Royal Commission on Agriculture.

s: Which committee recommended Krishi Vigyan Kendras in 1973?
x: The Mohan Singh Mehta committee (1973) led to the first KVK at Puducherry in 1974.

s: How many institutes are there in the ICAR network?
x: ICAR has 113 institutes, of which 72 are research institutes.

s: In which year was the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) set up?
x: ICFRE was set up in 1986 with HQ at Dehradun; 1906 is FRI's year.

s: Where is the Institute of Forest Biodiversity located?
x: The Institute of Forest Biodiversity is at Hyderabad; Jabalpur has the Tropical Forest Research Institute.

s: Where is the Tropical Forest Research Institute (TFRI) of ICFRE located?
x: TFRI is at Jabalpur.

s: Where is the Institute of Wood Science and Technology (IWST) located?
x: IWST is at Bengaluru.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM) located?
x: IIFM (1982) is at Bhopal; FRI and ICFRE headquarters are at Dehradun.

s: Where is the Institute of Forest Genetics and Tree Breeding (IFGTB) of ICFRE located?
x: IFGTB is at Coimbatore; TFRI is at Jabalpur, IWST at Bengaluru and RFRI at Jorhat.

s:
Match the following ICFRE institutes with their locations:
List-I

B. IFGTB
C. AFRI
D. RFRI
List-II
1. Jodhpur
2. Jorhat
3. Shimla

x: HFRI is at Shimla, IFGTB at Coimbatore, AFRI (arid forests) at Jodhpur and RFRI (rain forests) at Jorhat.

s: Where is the ICFRE Centre for Eco-Rehabilitation (CSFER) located?
x: CSFER (now FRCER), set up in 1992, is at Prayagraj; IFP is at Ranchi.

s:
Consider the following statements about parent departments:
1. ICMR functions under the Department of Health Research.
2. CSIR functions under the Department of Space.
3. ISRO functions under the Department of Space.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ICMR is under DHR and ISRO under the Department of Space; CSIR is under DSIR, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Under which department does the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) function?
x: DRDO is under the Department of Defence R&D (DDR&D), Ministry of Defence.

s: Where is the headquarters of ISRO located?
x: ISRO headquarters and the Department of Space secretariat are at Antariksh Bhavan, Bengaluru.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. ISRO is headquartered at Antariksh Bhavan, Bengaluru.
2. DRDO is headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: ISRO HQ is Antariksh Bhavan, Bengaluru, and DRDO HQ is DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi.

s: Through which instrument was the Department of Atomic Energy set up in 1954?
x: DAE was set up in 1954 by a Presidential Order, not an Act, and is directly under the Prime Minister.

s: In which year was the Atomic Energy Commission set up?
x: The Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Space Commission?
o: It is chaired by the Secretary, DoS, who is also the ISRO Chairman
It is associated with the Department of Space
The Department of Space reports to the Minister of Science and Technology
x: The Department of Space reports directly to the Prime Minister.

s: In which year was ISRO established?
x: ISRO came in 1969; INCOSPAR was formed in 1962 under Vikram Sarabhai and DAE.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Samir V. Kamat — Chairman of ISRO
Samir V. Kamat — Chairman of the Space Commission by virtue of heading DoS
x: V. Narayanan is the ISRO Chairman (Jan 2026). Samir V. Kamat is the DRDO Chairman and Secretary, DDR&D; the Space Commission is chaired by the Secretary, DoS, who is the ISRO Chairman.

s: Who chairs the Atomic Energy Commission ex officio?
x: The AEC (1948) is chaired ex officio by the Secretary, DAE.

s: Under whom was INCOSPAR, the forerunner of ISRO, set up in 1962?
x: INCOSPAR (1962) was set up under Vikram Sarabhai and DAE.

s: Which of the following correctly describes DRDO?
o: Headquartered at Hyderabad; conducts agricultural research
Headquartered at Bengaluru; plans space missions
Headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi; develops indigenous defence technology
Headquartered at Gandhinagar; regulates atomic energy
x: DRDO is headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi, and develops indigenous defence technology through its network of laboratories.

s: Where is the Indian Bureau of Mines headquartered?
x: IBM is at Nagpur; CIMFR is at Dhanbad and NATMO at Kolkata.

s: LVM3-M6, launched on 24 December 2025, carried which payload, the heaviest ever launched from India?
x: LVM3-M6 placed BlueBird Block-2 in orbit, described as the heaviest payload launched from India.

s: Where is IN-SPACe, the space regulator-promoter for private players, headquartered?
x: IN-SPACe (2020) is headquartered at Ahmedabad.

s: In which year was DRDO established?
x: DRDO was set up in 1958, with HQ at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ISRO's commercial and regulatory arms?
x: NSIL dates from 2019; Antrix was set up in September 1992.

s: Where is the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) located?
x: NRSC, the remote-sensing centre of ISRO, is at Hyderabad.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Indian Bureau of Mines is at Nagpur; the other three pairs are correct.

s: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), established in 1945 at Bombay, is associated with which development?
o: The production of rare earth minerals
The establishment of district-level agricultural extension centres
The beginning of organised nuclear research in India
x: TIFR was established in 1945 at Bombay and marked the beginning of organised nuclear research in India.

s: Which body is India's regulator for nuclear and radiation safety?
x: AERB regulates nuclear and radiation safety; IREL handles beach-sand minerals and the Heavy Water Board makes heavy water.

s: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre began in 1954 as the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay. After whom was it renamed in 1967?
x: AEET was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in 1967 in honour of Homi Jehangir Bhabha.

s: Which BARC reactor is fuelled by uranium-233?
x: KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor of the group; APSARA was Asia's first research reactor and Dhruva the largest.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IGCAR — fast breeder reactor research and development
NPCIL — exploration of uranium and thorium
IREL — operation of nuclear power reactors
x: IGCAR, Kalpakkam does fast breeder reactor R&D. The others are wrong: NPCIL builds and runs nuclear power plants. The Heavy Water Board, not AERB, produces heavy water, and AERB is the safety regulator. IREL handles beach-sand minerals and rare earths, not reactors.

s: Which of the following BARC or DAE products is correctly matched with its use or description?
x: Bhabhatron is a cobalt therapy unit. Nisargruna is a biogas plant, AKRUTI is a rural incubator and TAG refers to groundnut varieties.

s: Which was Asia's first research reactor, commissioned in 1956?
x: APSARA (1956) was Asia's first research reactor; Dhruva is the largest and KAMINI uses U-233.

s: Which DAE unit deals with beach-sand minerals and rare earths such as monazite?
x: IREL handles beach-sand minerals and rare earths.

s:
Consider the following statements about DAE reactors:
1. Dhruva is the largest research reactor.
2. KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor.
3. APSARA is Asia's first research reactor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Dhruva is the largest, KAMINI the only U-233-fuelled and APSARA Asia's first.

s: In NIRF 2025, what rank did Homi Bhabha National Institute (HBNI), the deemed university of DAE, get in the research category?
x: HBNI ranked 7th in research and 20th overall in NIRF 2025.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD)?
x: AMD, the DAE unit that explores atomic minerals, is headquartered at Hyderabad.

s: Which institution runs the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) near Pune?
x: GMRT near Pune is run by NCRA-TIFR, which is also India's lead for the Square Kilometre Array.

s: What is the total capacity of NPCIL's fleet of 23 nuclear reactors?
x: NPCIL's fleet is 23 reactors with 7,480 MW of capacity.

Arrange the following in chronological order of their setting up:
1. TIFR
2. Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (now BARC)
3. AERB
4. NPCIL
