x: TIFR 1945, AEET 1954, AERB 1983, NPCIL 1987.

s: Which ICMR institute is INCORRECTLY matched with its location?
o: National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis – Pune
x: NIRT is at Chennai, like NIE; Pune has NIV.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated foundations of ICMR's Strategic Plan and Vision 2030?
o: Alignment with the National Health Policy
Privatisation of all biomedical research institutions
x: The stated foundations are strengthening health research capacity, leveraging traditional medicine and aligning with the National Health Policy. Privatisation of all institutions is not included.

s: The ICMR National Institute of Nutrition (NIN) is located at:
x: NIN is at Hyderabad.

s: Where is the ICMR National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (NIRT) located?
x: NIRT is at Chennai, not Pune; Pune has NIV.

s: Where is the ICMR National Institute of Epidemiology (NIE) located?
x: NIE is at Chennai; NIV is at Pune and NIN at Hyderabad.

s: Where is the Army's Institute of Military Law located?
x: The Institute of Military Law is at Kamptee near Nagpur; Pune has the Institute of National Integration.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with an institution or facility in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NARL is located at Gadanki. SDSC-SHAR is at Sriharikota, NSTL is at Visakhapatnam and CTRI is at Rajahmundry.

s: Where is the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) located?
x: NIOT is at Thupilipallam, Nellore; Pedavegi, Eluru has IIOPR for oil palm research.

s: Where is the Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research (IIOPR) located?
x: IIOPR is at Pedavegi, Eluru.

s: What is the full form of IIOPR?
o: Indian Institute of Oilseeds and Pulses Research
Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research
Indian Institute of Organic Plant Research
Indian Institute of Oil and Petroleum Research
x: IIOPR is the Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research.

s: Where is the Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) located?
x: CTRI is at Rajahmundry; NIO has a regional centre at Visakhapatnam.

s: Where is NACIN located in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NACIN's campus is at Palasamudram near Hindupur; NARL is at Gadanki.

s: Who founded the Indian Science Congress Association in 1914?
x: ISCA was founded in 1914 by the British chemists J.L. Simonsen and P.S. MacMahon.

s: Where is the Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA) headquartered?
x: ISCA's headquarters is in Kolkata, not New Delhi.

s: Where was the 108th Indian Science Congress (January 2023) held?
x: The 108th session was held at RTM Nagpur University on S&T for sustainable development with women empowerment.

s: Who presided over the first session of the Indian Science Congress in 1914?
x: The first session (1914, Kolkata, Asiatic Society) was presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.

s: What was the theme of the 108th Indian Science Congress (2023)?
o: Science and Technology for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment
x: The 108th session at RTM Nagpur University had the theme of S&T for sustainable development with women empowerment.

s: Where was the first session of the Indian Science Congress held in 1914?
x: The first session met in 1914 at the Asiatic Society, Kolkata, presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.

s: The 109th Indian Science Congress was planned at which university, which later withdrew amid a DST-ISCA dispute?
x: The 109th session was planned at LPU in January 2024, but LPU withdrew amid the DST-ISCA dispute.

s: In which year did the India International Science Festival (IISF) begin?
x: IISF began in 2015 in New Delhi, organised by MoST and MoES with Vijnana Bharati.

s: In which year did C.V. Raman discover the Raman Effect, commemorated by National Science Day?
x: National Science Day commemorates C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.

s: Whose birth anniversary is commemorated by National Mathematics Day, declared in 2012?
x: National Mathematics Day commemorates Srinivasa Ramanujan's birth anniversary. It was declared in 2012, his 125th birth year.

s: What does National Technology Day, observed on 11 May, commemorate?
x: National Technology Day (11 May) marks the Pokhran-II tests of 1998 and was declared in 1999.

s: Where was the 11th India International Science Festival (December 2025) held?
x: The 11th IISF was held at Panchkula on 6-9 December 2025.

s: On which date is National Mathematics Day observed?
x: National Mathematics Day is on 22 December, Ramanujan's birthday, declared in 2012.

s: On which date is National Technology Day observed?
x: National Technology Day is on 11 May, marking the Pokhran-II tests of 1998.

s: Along with MoST and MoES, which organisation jointly organises the India International Science Festival?
x: IISF, begun in 2015, is organised by MoST and MoES with Vijnana Bharati.

s: What is Vigyan Dhara?
o: A DST umbrella scheme merging three schemes relating to capacity building, research and innovation
An autonomous body for grassroots innovations under NITI Aayog
A radio network operated by IGNOU
A single television channel for school education
x: Vigyan Dhara is a DST umbrella scheme merging schemes concerning S&T institutional and human capacity building, research and development, and innovation, technology development and deployment.

s: Vigyan Prasar, set up in 1989 at New Delhi, is an autonomous organisation of which body?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
x: Vigyan Prasar is an autonomous organisation of the Department of Science and Technology, Ministry of Science and Technology.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DD Science and India Science?
o: DD Science is a one-hour daily science slot on DD National
India Science is an Internet-based science channel
India Science is run by NCSM
x: India Science is run by Vigyan Prasar, not NCSM.

s: On which date were DD Science and India Science launched together?
x: The two Vigyan Prasar platforms were launched on 15 January 2019.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: SWAYAM Prabha — Group of free DTH educational channels
Gyan Darshan — Higher-education channel of UGC-CEC
Vyas — FM radio counterpart of Gyan Darshan
Gyan Vani — Group of free DTH educational channels
x: SWAYAM Prabha is a group of free DTH educational channels of the Ministry of Education. Vyas is the UGC-CEC higher-education channel, while Gyan Vani is the FM counterpart of Gyan Darshan.

s: Gyan Darshan, launched on 26 January 2000, is run by the MHRD with Prasar Bharati and which institution?
x: Gyan Darshan is run by the MHRD with IGNOU and Prasar Bharati; Vyas is the UGC-CEC channel.

s: SWAYAM Prabha, the free DTH educational service launched in 2017, has how many channels?
x: SWAYAM Prabha offers 32 free DTH channels under the Ministry of Education.

s: Which of the following launched Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (2015), which promotes inquiry-based learning of science and mathematics in schools?
o: Ministry of HRD (now Ministry of Education)
x: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of HRD, now the Ministry of Education.

s: The National Council for Science & Technology Communication (NCSTC) functions under which organisation?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
x: NCSTC is organised under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

s: The National Council of Science Museums is the nodal agency for which scheme of the Ministry of Culture?
o: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science
x: NCSM is the nodal agency for the Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS).

s: In which year was Science Express, DST's exhibition train, first flagged off?
x: Science Express, run by DST with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, was first flagged off in 2007.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: National Council of Science Museums – Ministry of Culture
x: NCSM, formed on 4 April 1978 with headquarters at Kolkata, is under the Ministry of Culture. Vigyan Prasar, Vigyan Rail and NIF are all linked to DST.

s: Who organised 'Vigyan Rail', a science exhibition on wheels run in 2003-04?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
x: Vigyan Rail was organised by the Department of Science and Technology (DST). CSIR is the classic trap (UPSC 2005). NCSM (Ministry of Culture) runs science centres and mobile exhibition buses, and the Ministry of HRD ran the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, not the science trains.

s: ICMR-SHINE, a science and health outreach initiative, is intended primarily for which group?
x: ICMR-SHINE, expanded as Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers, is an outreach initiative for students of Classes 9–12.

s: Where is the headquarters of the National Council of Science Museums?
x: NCSM (4 April 1978), under the Ministry of Culture, is headquartered at Kolkata.

s: Which body organises the National Children's Science Congress?
x: The National Children's Science Congress is run by NCSTC of DST; its 31st session was at Bhopal in 2025.

s: In which year was the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM) set up?
x: NCSM was set up on 4 April 1978 under the Ministry of Culture, with HQ at Kolkata.

s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the National Innovation Foundation?
o: Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan
National Biennial Grassroots Innovation and Traditional Knowledge Awards
VIGYANOTSAV quiz for National Science Day
x: The National Innovation Foundation conducts or is associated with the grassroots innovation awards, IGNITE and the Festival of Innovation at Rashtrapati Bhavan. VIGYANOTSAV is associated with National Science Day outreach by NCSTC.

s: From which network did the National Innovation Foundation grow?
x: NIF grew out of the Honey Bee Network, associated with Prof. Anil K. Gupta, SRISTI and IIM Ahmedabad.

s: With whose support was the National Innovation Foundation-India set up in March 2000?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
x: NIF-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of the Department of Science and Technology and functions as an autonomous body of DST.

s: Which body scouts, supports and spreads grassroots innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge?
x: This is the mandate of the National Innovation Foundation.

s: Where is the Festival of Innovation (FOIN), linked with the National Innovation Foundation, held?
x: NIF's Festival of Innovation is held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

s: Who started the Honey Bee Network, from which the National Innovation Foundation grew?
x: Prof. Anil K. Gupta (SRISTI, IIM Ahmedabad) started the Honey Bee Network, the origin of NIF.

s: Where is the National Innovation Foundation-India located?
x: NIF-India, set up in March 2000 as an autonomous body of DST, is at Gandhinagar.

s: Where is the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI) headquartered?
x: NASI is at Prayagraj, IASc at Bengaluru and INSA at New Delhi.

s: In which year was the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI) founded?
x: NASI was founded in 1930, IASc in 1934 and INSA in 1935.

s: Who founded the National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), India's oldest science academy, in 1930?
x: NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and is regarded as the oldest science academy in India.

s: Who founded the Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc), Bengaluru, in 1934?
x: C.V. Raman founded IASc in 1934; Meghnad Saha founded NASI in 1930.

s: Under what name was the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), New Delhi, originally founded in 1935?
o: National Institute of Sciences of India
x: INSA began in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India and was renamed in 1970.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian science academies:
1. NASI was founded before IASc.
2. INSA is headquartered at Bengaluru.
3. IASc was founded by C.V. Raman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NASI (1930) came before IASc (1934), which Raman founded; INSA is headquartered at New Delhi, not Bengaluru.

s: In which year was the National Institute of Sciences of India renamed the Indian National Science Academy (INSA)?
x: Founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India, it was renamed INSA in 1970.

s: The Smart India Hackathon is organised by the Innovation Cell of which body?
x: SIH is run with the Ministry of Education's Innovation Cell, with AICTE as partner since 2017.

s: Which body runs VIPNET, a network of science clubs?
x: VIPNET is Vigyan Prasar's network of science clubs.

s: Which one of the following programmes was launched through collaboration between CSIR and Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan in 2017?
x: JIGYASA was started through CSIR–Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan collaboration in 2017.

s: Which scheme, implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti, targets meritorious girl students of Classes 9 to 12?
x: Vigyan Jyoti targets meritorious girl students in Classes 9 to 12 and is implemented with the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti.

s: Which body runs WISE-KIRAN, which includes WISE-PhD, WISE-PDF and WIDUSHI?
x: WISE-KIRAN is a DST initiative for women scientists, especially those with career breaks.

s: Which DST scheme has set up STI Hubs for SC/ST communities?
x: SEED has set up STI Hubs for SC/ST communities; GATI works on institutional gender equity and CURIE on women PG colleges.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SERB-POWER — Women researchers in academic and R&D institutions
GATI — Women scientists returning to India from abroad
Vigyan Jyoti — Senior interdisciplinary women scientists
x: SERB-POWER (now under ANRF) gives research grants and fellowships to women researchers in academic and R&D institutions. The others are mismatched: BioCARe (DBT) supports women biotech scientists after a career break, GATI is the institutional gender-equity charter, and Vigyan Jyoti is for girl students of Classes 9-12.

s: Which body runs BioCARe, the scheme for women biotech scientists after a career break?
x: BioCARe is a DBT scheme; WISE-KIRAN is the DST career-break scheme.

s: For which group is WIDUSHI, under WISE-KIRAN, mainly meant?
o: Women scientists seeking their first extramural biotechnology grant
Senior women scientists conducting interdisciplinary research in science and technology
x: WIDUSHI is meant for senior women scientists engaged in interdisciplinary research in science and technology.

s: Which DST scheme gives research facilities to 22 women PG colleges?
x: CURIE of DST supports 22 women PG colleges with research facilities.

s: On which UK gender-equity charter is the DST's GATI modelled?
x: GATI (Gender Advancement for Transforming Institutions) targets institutions and is modelled on the UK's Athena SWAN charter.

s: Which of the following is a DST infrastructure-upgradation programme rather than a brain-gain scheme?
x: FIST upgrades infrastructure; VAJRA, Ramanujan Fellowship and INSPIRE aim at brain gain.

s: What is the full form of FIST, a DST scheme?
o: Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure
Facility for Innovation in Science and Technology
Fund for Innovation and Scientific Talent
Facility for Improvement of Scientific Training
x: FIST is the Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure in universities and higher institutions.

s: Which DST programme, begun in 2009, supports research only in universities?
x: PURSE (Promotion of University Research and Scientific Excellence) is university-only research support from 2009.

s: Which DST programme gives researchers access to costly analytical instruments through Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facilities?
x: SAIF stands for Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facilities, which give access to costly instruments.

s: What is the full form of SATHI, a DST programme?
o: Science and Technology Hubs for Innovation
Scientific Advancement through Technology and Human Innovation
Sophisticated Advanced Training and Help Institutes
x: SATHI = Sophisticated Analytical & Technical Help Institutes; they are shared, professionally run instrument facilities.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component associated with NIDHI?
x: NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is a separate startup-support programme associated with NCGTC.

s: Which of the following implements TIDE 2.0 (Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs), which supports ICT start-ups through incubators?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
x: TIDE 2.0 is a MeitY programme launched in 2019 to support ICT and technology start-ups through incubators.

s: NIDHI, launched in 2016, is an initiative of which department?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
x: NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the Department of Science and Technology.

s: What does the RDI Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 1 July 2025, provide?
x: The RDI Scheme provides ₹1 lakh crore over six years, steered by the ANRF Governing Board with DST as nodal department.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its body?
o: Fund of Funds for Startups – SIDBI
Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups – NCGTC
x: NIDHI (2016) is a DST initiative; the other three pairs are correct.

s: What is the full form of NIDHI?
o: National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations
National Investment for Development of High-tech Industries
National Innovation and Development Hub Initiative
New Initiative for Developing Home-grown Innovations
x: NIDHI, launched by DST in 2016, is the National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations.

s: What is the size of the Fund of Funds for Startups managed by SIDBI?
x: The Fund of Funds for Startups, run by SIDBI, has a corpus of ₹10,000 crore.

s: Where is the central hub of Andhra Pradesh's Ratan Tata Innovation Hub?
x: RTIH's central hub is at Mangalagiri (Amaravati) with spokes at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry, Vijayawada-Guntur, Tirupati and Anantapur.

s: Which body set up the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub as a Section-8 company?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS) set up RTIH, inaugurated on 20 August 2025.

s: How many Atal Tinkering Labs did Andhra Pradesh have in 2024-25?
x: Andhra Pradesh had 590 ATLs in 2024-25.

s: In which year was the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub of Andhra Pradesh inaugurated?
x: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub was inaugurated on 20 August 2025 by CM N. Chandrababu Naidu, with its central hub at Mangalagiri.

s: Which was the first State in India to launch an Innovation and Startup Policy (2014-2020)?
x: Andhra Pradesh was the first State to launch its Innovation and Startup Policy, for 2014-2020.

s: Which body is the nodal agency for implementing Startup initiatives in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Innovation Society (APIS), under the ITE&C Department and headed by a CEO, is the State's nodal agency for start-ups.

s: Which group does SEATS (Scheme for Early Attraction of Talents for Science) target?
x: SEATS targets school students; AORC concerns doctoral and post-doctoral careers.

s: What is the full form of MANAK, the INSPIRE component for school students of Classes VI-X?
o: Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge
Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge
Mission for Advancing National Aptitude and Knowledge
Model Awards for Nurturing Aspiring Kids
x: MANAK = Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge, for Classes VI-X (age 10-15). The other expansions are made up; 'Million Awards for National Academic Knowledge' is a common wrong guess.

s:
Consider the following statements about INSPIRE-SHE:
1. SHE stands for Scholarship for Higher Education.
2. It is meant for top-ranked UG and PG students in natural and basic sciences.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: SHE is the Scholarship for Higher Education for top UG and PG science students, so it targets higher education, not school students.

s: INSPIRE was launched in 2008 by which organisation as a flagship programme?
x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the Department of Science and Technology launched in 2008.

s: What is the full form of AORC (INSPIRE Fellowship and Faculty) in INSPIRE?
x: AORC is the Assured Opportunity for Research Careers, covering doctoral and post-doctoral researchers.

s: How much money does each selected student get under INSPIRE-MANAK?
x: INSPIRE-MANAK is for students of Classes VI-X (aged 10-15); each selected student gets ₹10,000.

s: About what share of the 653 INSPIRE doctoral fellowships given in 2025 went to women?
x: In 2025, 653 INSPIRE doctoral fellowships were given and about 65% went to women.

s: What was the rise in the allocation for Atal Tinkering Labs in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: The allocation for ATLs increased from ₹500 crore to ₹3,200 crore in the Union Budget 2026–27.

s: Under the Atal Innovation Mission, which component focuses on rural and underserved areas?
x: ACICs focus on rural and underserved areas; ATLs are in schools and AICs support start-ups.

s: For students of which grades are Atal Tinkering Labs set up?
x: ATLs are established in schools for students of grades 6–12.

s: Which State was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0?
x: Tripura was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0.

s: What is the outlay of Atal Innovation Mission 2.0, approved in 2024?
x: AIM 2.0 has Rs 2,750 crore and runs till March 2028. Rs 500 crore to Rs 3,200 crore is the 2026-27 Budget rise for Atal Tinkering Labs, and Rs 10,000 crore is the SIDBI Fund of Funds for Startups.

s: Which group is ARISE, under the Atal Innovation Mission, meant for?
x: ARISE (Atal Research and Innovation for Small Enterprises) targets MSMEs; ACICs serve rural areas.

s: Under which body was the Atal Innovation Mission set up in 2016?
x: The Atal Innovation Mission is the flagship of NITI Aayog, set up in 2016; it is not a DST scheme.

s: Which component of the Atal Innovation Mission supports start-ups in universities and institutions?
x: Atal Incubation Centres (AICs) support start-ups; ATLs are for schools, ACICs for rural areas and ARISE for MSMEs.

s: How many Atal Tinkering Labs have been set up across 700+ districts of India?
x: About 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs have been set up in schools across 700+ districts.

s: Under AIM 2.0, what are the LIPI centres meant for?
o: Innovation in the 22 scheduled languages through vernacular innovation centres
x: AIM 2.0 plans 30 vernacular innovation centres (LIPI) in the 22 scheduled languages.

s: In which city was the India-France ATL Bridge launched in June 2026?
x: The India-France ATL Bridge was launched at Nice during Bharat Innovates 2026.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme or initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST)?
x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a DBT (Department of Biotechnology) scheme for Indian life-science and biotech scientists abroad who return, so it is the odd one out. INSPIRE, Vigyan Jyoti and the Nano Mission are DST schemes.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: PMRF – Women scientists returning after a career break
VAJRA – Overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs
J.C. Bose Fellowship – Active senior scientists
x: PMRF is for PhD scholars in IITs, IISc, IISERs and other top institutions and is administered by the Ministry of Education, not a career-break scheme.

s: In connection with which occasion was the Swarnajayanti Fellowship begun?
o: The centenary of the Indian Science Congress
x: The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark 50 years of India’s Independence and supports young scientists with a proven record.

s: Which body runs the Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF), started in 2018?
x: PMRF is a Ministry of Education scheme for PhD scholars in IITs, IISc and IISERs.

s: Which body awards the Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship for life-science returnees?
x: Ramalingaswami is a DBT (not DST) fellowship for life-science and biotech returnees only.

s: Who are the target group of the Ramanujan Fellowship?
o: Senior women scientists in interdisciplinary research
Indian scientists working abroad who wish to return to India
PhD scholars in IITs, IISc and IISERs
School students of Classes VI to X
x: The Ramanujan Fellowship (SERB, now ANRF) is for Indian scientists abroad who return to work in India; it is a brain-gain scheme.

s: Which of the following schemes brings overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs, to Indian institutions for short spells?
x: VAJRA (Visiting Advanced Joint Research Faculty) of SERB/ANRF brings overseas scientists, including NRIs and OCIs, to India for short spells; it is a brain-gain scheme.

s: What is the full form of PMECRG, a scheme of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
o: PM Excellence in Core Research Grant
x: PMECRG is the PM Early Career Research Grant, one of the ANRF schemes.

s: Where is the supercomputer Pratyush located?
x: Pratyush is at IITM Pune; Mihir is at NCMRWF Noida, Flosolver at NAL Bengaluru and Anupam at BARC.

s: Which was India's first supercomputer, developed by C-DAC in 1991?
x: PARAM 8000 (1991) was built by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar and was India's first supercomputer. PARAM Shivay (2019) was the first NSM machine, Anupam is a BARC machine, and AIRAWAT is the later AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune.

s: Where is the weather supercomputer Mihir located?
x: Mihir is at NCMRWF Noida; Pratyush is at IITM Pune.

s: Which organisation developed the Flosolver supercomputer?
x: Flosolver was developed by NAL Bengaluru; Anupam is BARC's machine.

s: For which of the following is Vijay Bhatkar known?
o: Architect of the Deep Ocean Mission
Founder of India’s quantum communication mission
Chairperson of the ANRF Governing Board
x: Vijay Bhatkar is recognised as the father of Indian supercomputing.

s: Along with C-DAC, which institution implements the National Supercomputing Mission (2015)?
x: NSM, run by DST and MeitY, is implemented by C-DAC and IISc Bengaluru, not IIT Bombay.

s: Where is the supercomputer PARAM Shivay hosted?
x: PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU) Varanasi; PARAM Brahma is at IISER Pune, PARAM Pravega at IISc and PARAM Ganga at IIT Roorkee.

s: Which supercomputer under the National Supercomputing Mission is hosted at IIT Roorkee?
x: PARAM Ganga is at IIT Roorkee; PARAM Brahma is at IISER Pune, PARAM Pravega at IISc and PARAM Shivay at IIT (BHU).

s: Where is the supercomputer PARAM Brahma, set up under the National Supercomputing Mission, hosted?
x: PARAM Brahma is hosted at IISER Pune; PARAM Ganga is at IIT Roorkee and PARAM Shivay at IIT (BHU).

s: Which of the following institutions jointly steers the National Supercomputing Mission?
x: The mission is jointly steered by the Department of Science and Technology and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

s:
Consider the following statements about AIRAWAT:
1. It is an artificial-intelligence supercomputer associated with the National Supercomputing Mission.
2. It is located at NCMRWF, Noida.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AIRAWAT is the NSM's AI supercomputer, but it is located at C-DAC, Pune, not NCMRWF Noida.

s: Where is the supercomputer PARAM Pravega hosted?
x: PARAM Pravega is at IISc Bengaluru; PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: PARAM Kamrupa is hosted at IIT Guwahati. PARAM Shakti is at IIT Madras, PARAM Rudra systems are at Pune, Delhi and Kolkata, and AIRAWAT is at C-DAC, Pune.

s: What does 'Rudra' refer to in the National Supercomputing Mission?
o: The interconnect used in all PARAM systems
A C-DAC high-performance computing chip programme
A server board on which the Rudra machines are built
x: The Rudra machines are built on the Rudra server; AUM is the separate C-DAC HPC chip programme.

s: Where is PARAM Porul, commissioned in May 2022 under the NSM, hosted?
x: PARAM Porul is at NIT Tiruchirappalli; PARAM Ananta is at IIT Gandhinagar.

s: Where is the supercomputer PARAM Ananta hosted?
x: PARAM Ananta, a National Supercomputing Mission system, is hosted at IIT Gandhinagar.

s: Which Indian supercomputer was ranked 75th in the Top500 list released at ISC 2023 in Germany?
x: AIRAWAT, the AI supercomputer at C-DAC Pune, was ranked 75th in the Top500 at ISC 2023 (May 2023).

s: What is the name of the indigenous interconnect used in India's NSM supercomputers?
x: The indigenous NSM stack uses the Rudra server board and the Trinetra interconnect; AUM is C-DAC's HPC chip programme.

s: How many supercomputing systems were planned under the National Supercomputing Mission?
x: The NSM planned 40 systems with more than 64 petaflops; 37 have been commissioned.

s: Over which network are the machines of the National Supercomputing Mission linked as the National Supercomputing Grid?
x: NSM machines are linked on the National Supercomputing Grid over the National Knowledge Network.

s: Which of the following is NOT a site of the three PARAM Rudra supercomputers?
x: The three PARAM Rudra systems are at Pune (GMRT), Delhi (IUAC) and Kolkata (S.N. Bose Centre); IIT Gandhinagar hosts PARAM Ananta.

s: Which department implements the National Quantum Mission, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31?
x: The National Quantum Mission is under DST, with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore over eight years (2023–24 to 2030–31).

s: How many physical qubits are the intermediate-scale quantum computers under the National Quantum Mission meant to have?
x: The target is intermediate-scale computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits within eight years.

s: Which of the following is NOT a target of the National Quantum Mission?
o: Satellite QKD over 2000 km within India
Development of magnetometers and atomic clocks
Intermediate-scale quantum computers of 50-1000 physical qubits
Indigenous Rudra server boards for supercomputers
x: The Rudra server board belongs to the National Supercomputing Mission; QKD, quantum sensing and 50-1000 qubit computers are NQM targets.

s: Which of the following National Quantum Mission thematic hubs is wrongly matched with its host?
o: Quantum Materials and Devices – IIT Madras
Quantum Sensing and Metrology – IIT Bombay
x: The Quantum Materials and Devices hub is hosted by IIT Delhi, not IIT Madras; IIT Madras hosts the Quantum Communication hub.

s: On which date did the Union Cabinet approve the National Quantum Mission?
x: The Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission on 19 April 2023 with ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.

s: Which property lets a qubit be 0 and 1 at the same time?
x: Through superposition a qubit can be 0 and 1 together; this makes it the basic unit of quantum computing.

s: QNu Labs, a start-up backed under the National Quantum Mission, works in which area?
x: QNu Labs works on quantum key distribution (QKD); QpiAI built a 64-qubit QPU.

s: Which is the nodal ministry of the Deep Ocean Mission?
x: The Deep Ocean Mission is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, approved in June 2021.

s: To what depth is Matsya 6000, India's crewed submersible, designed to take three people?
x: Matsya 6000, built by NIOT Chennai, carries 3 people to 6,000 m.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission:
1. It has an outlay of ₹4,077 crore for five years.
2. Samudrayaan is a sub-project of the mission.
3. Matsya 6000 is being built by NIO Goa.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The mission has ₹4,077 crore for five years and includes Samudrayaan; Matsya 6000 is built by NIOT Chennai.

s: Which institute is building Matsya 6000, India's crewed submersible?
x: Matsya 6000 is built by NIOT Chennai under the Deep Ocean Mission; it is to take 3 people to 6,000 m.

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Development of Ocean Climate Change Advisory Services
Advanced Marine Station for Ocean Biology
Energy and Freshwater from the Ocean
x: The six components include deep-sea mining and a manned submersible, ocean climate change advisory services, deep-sea biodiversity, deep ocean survey, energy and freshwater from the ocean, and a marine station for ocean biology; ice-core drilling is not one.

s: The Deep Ocean Mission component 'Energy and Freshwater from the Ocean' plans offshore desalination powered by which technology?
x: It plans offshore desalination plants powered by Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC).

s:
Consider the following statements about India's Deep Ocean Mission:
1. It was approved in June 2021 with an outlay of Rs 4,077 crore.
2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Deep Ocean Mission was approved in June 2021 at Rs 4,077 crore and is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

s: Which body implements India's Deep Ocean Mission?
x: The Deep Ocean Mission (June 2021, Rs 4,077 crore) is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

s: What is MATSYA-6000, tested under India's Deep Ocean Mission?
x: MATSYA-6000 is the crewed submersible of India's Deep Ocean Mission (MoES), meant to reach 6,000 m depth.

s: What is the name of the deep-sea mining machine trialled at 5,270 m under India's Deep Ocean Mission?
x: The mining machine Varaha was trialled at 5,270 m; MATSYA-6000 is the crewed submersible.

s: NM-ICPS provides for how many Technology Innovation Hubs set up as Section-8 companies?
x: NM-ICPS provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs as Section-8 companies in host institutes.

s: On which area does the NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub at IISER Tirupati focus?
x: The IISER Tirupati TIH, IITTNiF, is associated with Positioning and Precision Technologies.

s: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) was approved by the Union Cabinet in which year and with what outlay?
x: NM-ICPS was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 December 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore for five years and sets up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs. Rs 6,003.65 crore (2023) is the National Quantum Mission and Rs 10,371.92 crore (2024) is the IndiaAI Mission.

s: What is the outlay of the IndiaAI Mission approved in 2024?
x: The IndiaAI Mission (2024) has an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore; ₹6,003.65 crore is the National Quantum Mission.

s: In the Bio-E3 Policy (2024), Bio-E3 stands for Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and what?
x: Bio-E3 means Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment; its core aim is a bio-manufacturing ecosystem.

s: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over which amount in 2024?
x: India’s bioeconomy was valued at over US$165 billion in 2024.

s: Which department steers the Bio-E3 Policy, approved by the Cabinet on 24 August 2024?
x: Bio-E3 is steered by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT).

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the infrastructure planned under the Bio-E3 Policy?
x: Bio-E3 plans biomanufacturing hubs, Bio-AI hubs and biofoundries; Technology Innovation Hubs belong to NM-ICPS.

s: Which of the following is NOT a thematic sector of the Bio-E3 Policy?
x: Bio-E3's six sectors are bio-based chemicals and enzymes, smart proteins, precision biotherapeutics, climate-resilient agriculture, carbon capture, and marine and space research.

s: What is the outlay of Biopharma SHAKTI announced in the Union Budget 2026-27?
x: Biopharma SHAKTI, for biologics and biosimilars, has ₹10,000 crore over 5 years (Budget 2026-27).

s: Who is the ex officio President of the Governing Board of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)?
o: The Union Minister of Science and Technology
x: Under the ANRF Act, 2023 the Prime Minister is the ex officio President of the ANRF Governing Board (the ANRF subsumed SERB).

s: Through which structure is the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund linked to the ANRF?
x: ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a two-tier Special Purpose Fund.

s: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation subsumed which body?
x: The ANRF, created by the ANRF Act 2023, subsumed SERB.

s: In which year was the Act creating the Anusandhan National Research Foundation passed?
x: ANRF was created by the ANRF Act, 2023.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches a mission with its ministry and outlay?
x: The IndiaAI Mission is under MeitY with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore. Semicon India is under MeitY with ₹76,000 crore, NQM is under DST with ₹6,003.65 crore, and NM-ICPS is under DST.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Quantum Mission is under MeitY.
2. Semicon India is under MeitY with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Semicon India is a MeitY mission of ₹76,000 crore; the National Quantum Mission's nodal department is DST, not MeitY.

s: Under which department, through the Survey of India, is the National Geospatial Mission announced in Budget 2025-26?
x: The National Geospatial Mission is under DST (Survey of India) and runs till 2031.

s: How many GPUs are planned under the IndiaAI Mission?
x: The IndiaAI Mission (MeitY, 2024, ₹10,371.92 crore) provides for 10,000+ GPUs.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Amaravati Quantum Valley is an Andhra Pradesh initiative. IITTNiF is associated with IISER Tirupati, PARAM Shivay with IIT (BHU) Varanasi, and the India-France ATL Bridge was launched at Nice.

s: Where is the 1Q Quantum Test and Reference Facility in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The 1Q facility is at Medha Towers, Gannavaram, while the 1S test bed is at SRM University-AP.

s: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at which of the following places?
x: The foundation stone of the Amaravati Quantum Valley was laid at Uddandarayunipalem.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the incentives in the Amaravati Quantum Valley?
o: Andhra Pradesh plans to train 4.5 million people in AI and quantum technologies
Technology firms get 100% exemption from stamp duty
Technology firms get 100% exemption from registration fees
The exemption applies only to registration fees and not to stamp duty
x: The policy gives 100% exemption from both stamp duty and registration fees, so saying it excludes stamp duty is wrong.

s: Where are classes of MeitY's NIELIT Quantum and AI campus, Amaravati, scheduled to begin in September 2026?
x: The NIELIT campus (Ministry of Electronics and IT) is to start classes from September 2026 at Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur.

s: Which was the first State in India to have a dedicated quantum computing policy?
x: Andhra Pradesh is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make Amaravati Quantum Valley a top-five global quantum hub by 2030.

s: Where is the 1S Quantum Reference Facility test bed in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The 1S test bed is at SRM University-AP; the 1Q test bed is at Medha Towers, Gannavaram.

s: India's first Quantum Reference Facility test beds in Andhra Pradesh were opened on 14 April 2026. Which day is observed on 14 April?
x: 14 April is World Quantum Day; the test beds were opened on that day in 2026.

s: Under the MoUs for Amaravati Quantum Valley (Feb 2026), which company is to train 1 lakh youth?
x: Among the seven MoUs of February 2026, IBM agreed to train 1 lakh youth.

s: Who is known as the Father of Quantum Theory?
x: Max Planck is the Father of Quantum Theory; Bohr is the Father of Atomic Physics, Raman of Indian Physics and Bhabha of India's nuclear programme.

s: The scientist Henri Becquerel was associated with which country?
x: Becquerel was French; Marie Curie was associated with both Poland and France.

s: With which institution was J.J. Thomson associated?
x: J.J. Thomson worked at the Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge; Chicago and Columbia are linked with Fermi.

s: Who is known as the 'Architect of the Nuclear Age'?
x: Enrico Fermi is called the architect of the nuclear age; Michael Faraday is known as the father of electricity.

s: Albert Einstein was associated with which of the following institutions?
x: Einstein worked at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study; Rutherford was at the Cavendish Laboratory and Manchester, and Bohr at Copenhagen.

s: Who explained the hydrogen spectrum?
x: Bohr explained the hydrogen spectrum; Planck explained black-body radiation, Einstein the photoelectric effect and Maxwell unified electromagnetism.

s: Who is known as the man who 'weighed the Earth'?
x: Henry Cavendish is called the man who weighed the Earth; Oppenheimer is the father of the atomic bomb and Bohr of atomic physics.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Galileo Galilei – Father of Experimental Physics
Isaac Newton – Father of Classical Mechanics
Albert Einstein – Father of Modern Physics
x: Rutherford is the Father of Nuclear Physics; the Father of Relativity is Albert Einstein.

s: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
o: Albert Einstein moved from Germany to Switzerland to the USA.
Enrico Fermi moved from Italy to the USA.
x: Niels Bohr was Danish, working in Copenhagen, not German.

s: Who is known as the Father of Nuclear Physics?
x: Rutherford is the Father of Nuclear Physics; Fermi is the Architect of the Nuclear Age and Oppenheimer the Father of the atomic bomb.

s: To which country did Niels Bohr, the Father of Atomic Physics, belong?
x: Bohr was Danish (Copenhagen), not German.

s: Who discovered radioactivity in 1896?
x: Henri Becquerel of France discovered radioactivity in 1896.

s: Who is known as the Father of Electricity?
x: Michael Faraday is called the Father of Electricity; Maxwell unified electromagnetism.

s: Who unified electricity and magnetism into one theory of electromagnetism?
x: James Clerk Maxwell unified electromagnetism.

s: Who is known as the 'Father of the atomic bomb'?
x: Oppenheimer is called the Father of the atomic bomb; Fermi is the Architect of the Nuclear Age.

s: Who named the elements oxygen and hydrogen?
x: Lavoisier, the Father of Modern Chemistry, named oxygen (1778) and hydrogen (1783).

s: The Raman Effect was discovered by C.V. Raman on 28 February 1928 at which institution?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata
x: C.V. Raman discovered the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the honours received by C. V. Raman?
o: Nobel Prize in 1930, Bharat Ratna in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
Nobel Prize in 1954, Bharat Ratna in 1929 and knighthood in 1930
Nobel Prize in 1929, Bharat Ratna in 1930 and knighthood in 1954
FRS in 1930, Padma Bhushan in 1954 and knighthood in 1929
x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.

s: In which year did C.V. Raman found the Indian Academy of Sciences?
x: Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.

s: What does the Raman Effect refer to?
o: Emission of electrons from a metal by light
Thermal ionisation of atoms in stars
Change in wavelength of scattered light
x: The Raman Effect is the change in wavelength of scattered light, discovered on 28 February 1928.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about C.V. Raman?
o: He was the first Indian director of IISc
He founded the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics
He first studied the harmonic nature of tabla and mridangam
x: The Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics was founded by Meghnad Saha; the other statements about Raman are true.

s: On which date is National Science Day observed in India?
x: National Science Day (28 February) marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928.

s: In which year did C.V. Raman found the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru?
x: Raman founded the Raman Research Institute in 1948; he founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bhabha's three-stage nuclear power programme – Uranium-based
First UN Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy – Geneva
Geneva Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy – 1955
President of the 1955 Geneva conference – Homi Bhabha
x: Bhabha's three-stage programme is thorium-based, not uranium-based; he presided over the first UN Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy at Geneva in 1955.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Atomic Energy Commission — First chairman, Homi Bhabha, 1948
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre — Founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945
x: The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966. It was not founded as BARC in 1945.

s: In which year was the Atomic Energy Commission, with Homi Bhabha as its first chairman, set up?
x: The AEC was set up in 1948 with Bhabha as first chairman; TIFR dates from 1945.

s: In which year was the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (1954), renamed BARC?
x: AEET was renamed BARC in 1967, after Bhabha died in the 1966 Air India crash.

s: Between which particles does Bhabha scattering take place?
x: Bhabha scattering is electron-positron scattering; Bhabha also gave the cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers.

s: Which honour did Homi Bhabha receive in 1942?
x: Bhabha won the Adams Prize in 1942; his Padma Bhushan came in 1954.

s: In which year did Homi Bhabha die in the Air India crash on Mont Blanc?
x: Bhabha died in 1966; AEET Trombay was renamed BARC in 1967 in his honour.

s: Which Indian scientist gave the cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers?
x: Homi Bhabha worked on cosmic rays and gave the cascade theory of cosmic-ray showers.

s: Who made the Jarvik-7 artificial heart?
x: Robert Jarvik made the Jarvik-7 artificial heart; Hans Berger developed the EEG.

s: Who invented Biorock reef technology?
x: Wolf Hilbertz invented Biorock technology; Robert Jarvik made the Jarvik-7 artificial heart.

s: Who invented the cathode ray tube?
x: Karl Ferdinand Braun invented the cathode ray tube; he shared the 1909 Physics Nobel with Marconi.

s: Who invented the EEG (electroencephalograph)?
x: Hans Berger invented the EEG, which records the electrical activity of the brain.

s: Who gave the name 'vitamin'?
x: Casimir Funk, a Polish biochemist, coined the name 'vitamin'.

s: Who developed the hybridoma technique for making monoclonal antibodies?
x: Georges Köhler and César Milstein developed the hybridoma technique.

s: By what name is the number 1729 popularly known?
x: The number 1729 is known as the Hardy-Ramanujan number.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.N. Bose — Quantum statistics and bosons
Birbal Sahni — Engineering and Diwan of Mysore
x: S.N. Bose is associated with quantum statistics and bosons. Prafulla Chandra Ray worked in chemistry, Birbal Sahni in palaeobotany, and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar with CSIR.

s: From which of his theories did Meghnad Saha formulate the Saha equation?
x: Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of thermal ionisation of elements.

s: Who named the particle class 'bosons' after S.N. Bose?
x: Paul Dirac coined the name 'bosons'; Bose had sent his paper 'Planck's Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta' to Einstein (1924).

s: To whom did Rabindranath Tagore dedicate his only science book, Visva-Parichay?
x: Rabindranath Tagore dedicated *Visva-Parichay*, published in 1937, to S. N. Bose.

s: Who translated S.N. Bose's 1924 paper 'Planck's Law and the Hypothesis of Light Quanta' into German?
x: Einstein translated the paper for Zeitschrift fur Physik, giving Bose-Einstein statistics; Dirac named the bosons.

s: In which year did S.N. Bose receive the Padma Vibhushan?
x: S.N. Bose got the Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and became FRS in 1958.

s: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked at Cambridge with which mathematician?
x: Srinivasa Ramanujan worked with the British mathematician G.H. Hardy at Cambridge.

s: On which date is National Mathematics Day, marking the birthday of Srinivasa Ramanujan, observed?
x: Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887, and that date is observed as National Mathematics Day.

s: Which anniversary of Ramanujan was marked by observing 2012 as National Mathematical Year?
x: 2012 marked the 125th birth anniversary of Ramanujan (born 1887).

s: Where was Srinivasa Ramanujan born on 22 December 1887?
x: Ramanujan was born at Erode, Tamil Nadu; Chidambaram is Ramakrishnan's birthplace.

s: What is the title of the 2015 British biopic on Srinivasa Ramanujan?
x: 'The Man Who Knew Infinity' (2015), based on Robert Kanigel's 1991 book, starred Dev Patel as Ramanujan.

s: With which of the following is Srinivasa Ramanujan's work associated?
x: Ramanujan worked on number theory, partitions, infinite series, continued fractions and mock theta functions.

s: What does the Saha equation help to determine, making it a basic tool for reading stellar spectra?
o: Distance and magnetic field of oceans
Temperature and ionisation state of stars
Age and chemical composition of plants
Mass and rotation of planets only
x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the temperature and ionisation state of stars.

s: For which project did Meghnad Saha, regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India, prepare the original plan?
x: Meghnad Saha prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.

s: Which institution was founded by Meghnad Saha in 1930?
o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science
x: Saha founded NASI in 1930; the Indian Academy of Sciences (1934) was Raman's.

s: In which year was Meghnad Saha elected to the Lok Sabha?
x: Saha, chief architect of river planning, was elected to the Lok Sabha in 1952.

s: Which Indian scientist devised an instrument to measure the weight and pressure of solar rays?
x: Meghnad Saha devised an instrument to measure the weight and pressure of solar rays.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Homi Bhabha and S. N. Bose?
o: S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1941
Homi Bhabha received the Padma Bhushan in 1954
S. N. Bose received the Padma Vibhushan in 1954
Homi Bhabha became an FRS in 1941
x: S. N. Bose became an FRS in 1958; it was Homi Bhabha who became an FRS in 1941.

s: Which group of scientists all worked at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata?
o: Homi Bhabha, Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan and C.V. Raman
J.C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S.N. Bose and C.V. Raman
Vikram Sarabhai, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Raja Ramanna and S.N. Bose
Srinivasa Ramanujan, Birbal Sahni, Homi Bhabha and Meghnad Saha
x: J.C. Bose, Meghnad Saha, S.N. Bose and C.V. Raman all worked at IACS.

s: Who developed the high-yield 'Super Rice' as chief breeder at IRRI, Philippines?
x: G.S. Khush, a plant geneticist, was chief breeder at IRRI from 1989 and developed high-yield 'Super Rice'.

s: Who served as the Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1919?
x: The engineer M. Visvesvaraya was Diwan of Mysore from 1912 to 1919.

s: Which of the following institutions was established in 1945?
x: TIFR was founded in 1945; the Bose Institute dates from 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences from 1934 and the Raman Research Institute from 1948.

s: Who founded the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), Kolkata, in 1876?
x: IACS was founded in Kolkata in 1876 by Mahendra Lal Sircar.

s: Which institute runs the Radio Astronomy Centre at Ooty?
x: TIFR, founded by Homi Bhabha in 1945, runs the Radio Astronomy Centre at Ooty (Ooty Radio Telescope).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about early Indian women scientists?
o: Kamala Sohonie was the first woman to obtain a D.Sc. from an Indian university
Anandibai Joshi earned an MD in Western medicine in 1886
Kamala Sohonie was the first woman admitted to IISc
Asima Chatterjee obtained a D.Sc. from Calcutta University in 1944
x: The first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university was Asima Chatterjee (Calcutta, 1944), not Kamala Sohonie.

s: Who was the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress (1975)?
x: Asima Chatterjee, also the first woman D.Sc. of an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944), became the first woman General President of the Indian Science Congress in 1975.

s: Anna Mani is popularly known as the ‘Weather Woman of India’ primarily because of her work in which field?
o: Meteorological instruments, solar radiation and wind energy
Cosmic rays, mesons and particle detectors
x: Anna Mani contributed to making India self-reliant in meteorological instruments and worked on solar radiation and wind energy. She also served as Deputy Director-General of the India Meteorological Department.

s: Who was the first Indian woman to obtain a Western medicine degree (MD, Pennsylvania, 1886)?
x: Anandibai Joshi took an MD in Pennsylvania in 1886; Sohonie was the first woman science PhD (1939).

s: Hybrids of which crop is Janaki Ammal, the plant breeding pioneer at Coimbatore, known for developing?
x: Janaki Ammal developed sugarcane hybrids at Coimbatore.

s: Who was the first woman to receive a D.Sc. from an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944)?
x: Asima Chatterjee took the first women's D.Sc. from Calcutta in 1944; Sohonie's 1939 Cambridge PhD is a different first.

s: In 2019, the IAU named the star HD 86081 'Bibha' after which particle physicist?
x: The star was named after Bibha Chowdhuri, who did cosmic-ray work with D.M. Bose.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kamala Sohonie:
1. She was the first Indian woman to get a PhD in a science discipline (Cambridge, 1939).
2. She was the first woman admitted to IISc.
3. She developed the anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are true; Ayush-56 was developed by Asima Chatterjee.

s: Who among the following developed the anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56?
x: Asima Chatterjee, an organic chemist and the first woman D.Sc. from an Indian university, developed Ayush-56.

s: In which year was botanist Janaki Ammal awarded the Padma Shri?
x: Janaki Ammal, known for sugarcane hybrids at Coimbatore, received the Padma Shri in 1977.

s: J.C. Bose was a pioneer in microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and used which of the following components?
x: J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.

s: Which one of the following is a book written by J.C. Bose?
o: The Mathematical Theory of Black Holes
x: The Nervous Mechanism of Plants was written by J.C. Bose. His other listed works include Response in the Living and Non-Living and the Bengali science-fiction work Niruddesher Kahini.

s: In which year did J.C. Bose found the Bose Institute, Kolkata?
x: J.C. Bose, who showed that plants respond to stimuli, founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata in 1917.

s: Crescograph was invented by whom?
x: J.C. Bose invented the crescograph to measure tiny plant growth and responses. Köhler and Milstein made hybridomas and Funk named vitamins.

s: Who wrote the Bengali science-fiction story 'Niruddesher Kahini'?
x: J.C. Bose wrote the Bengali sci-fi story Niruddesher Kahini, besides 'Response in the Living and Non-Living'.

s: Who wrote the book 'Response in the Living and Non-Living' (1902)?
x: J.C. Bose wrote 'Response in the Living and Non-Living' (1902) on how plants and metals respond to stimuli.

s: In which year was J.C. Bose elected a Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS)?
x: J.C. Bose became an FRS in 1920; he was knighted in 1917.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
o: He is called the 'Missile Man of India'
He was project director of SLV-3, which put Rohini in orbit in 1980
He led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
He was the 11th President of India from 2007 to 2012
x: Kalam was the 11th President from 2002 to 2007, not 2007 to 2012.

s: Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Indian Head of State to do which of the following?
x: Kalam was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft.

s: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was project director of which launch vehicle that put Rohini in orbit in 1980?
x: Kalam was project director of SLV-3, which placed Rohini in orbit in 1980.

s: With whom did Kalam write his autobiography 'Wings of Fire' (1999)?
x: Wings of Fire was written with Arun Tiwari; Ajay Rathore was his co-pilot on the Sukhoi-30 MKI flight.

s: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was chief executive of which programme that developed Agni?
x: Kalam was chief executive of IGMDP, which developed Agni.

s: Who was the first Indian woman to fly in a fighter aircraft (Sukhoi-30, 25 November 2009)?
x: President Pratibha Patil flew the Sukhoi-30 in 2009, after Kalam's 2006 flight.

s: With whom is Pokhran-II associated?
o: Anil Kakodkar and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
x: Pokhran-II was led by Kakodkar and Kalam; Pokhran-I (1974) was Raja Ramanna's.

s: In which year did INCOSPAR, headed by Vikram Sarabhai from 1962, become ISRO?
x: INCOSPAR became ISRO in 1969, and Sarabhai served as ISRO's first Chairman until his death in 1971.

s: Which institution was founded by Vikram Sarabhai in Ahmedabad in 1947?
x: Vikram Sarabhai founded the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad in 1947. The Community Science Centre was established in 1965, while TERLS was set up near Thiruvananthapuram.

s: Who was the first Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)?
x: Vikram Sarabhai was the first Chairman of ISRO. Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash and U.R. Rao are other prominent figures associated with India’s space programme.

s: For whom was the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal constituted in 1990?
o: Scientists working exclusively in marine biology
x: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal, constituted in 1990 by COSPAR and ISRO, recognises space scientists from developing countries.

s: Who became the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian to win the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026?
x: Annapurni Subramaniam won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026, becoming the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian recipient.

s: What was the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS), founded by Sarabhai in 1962, renamed?
x: TERLS was renamed the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre; SHAR is named after Satish Dhawan.

s: In which year did Vikram Sarabhai found the Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad?
x: The Community Science Centre came in 1965; PRL in 1947, TERLS in 1962 and ISRO in 1969.

s: What was the name of the Chandrayaan-2 lander, named after the father of India's space programme?
x: The Chandrayaan-2 lander was named 'Vikram' after Vikram Sarabhai; Pragyan was the rover.

s: In which year did Vikram Sarabhai become Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission?
x: Vikram Sarabhai became AEC Chairman in 1966, after Homi Bhabha's death; he was also first ISRO Chairman.

s: In which year was Vikram Sarabhai awarded the Padma Vibhushan (posthumously)?
x: Sarabhai died in 1971 and received the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in 1972; he got the Padma Bhushan in 1966.

s: Why is Tessy Thomas popularly known as the 'Missile Woman'?
o: The Agni-IV project as its project director
The Rohini satellite as its project director
x: Tessy Thomas of DRDO was the project director of Agni-IV and is popularly known as the “Missile Woman.”

s: After whom is the Sriharikota launch centre SHAR named?
x: SHAR is named after ISRO Chairman Satish Dhawan, associated with Aryabhata.

s: Who was the first Indian inducted into the Satellite Hall of Fame?
x: U.R. Rao, ISRO Chairman 1984-94, was the first Indian in the Satellite Hall of Fame.

s: Which document is K. Kasturirangan, ISRO Chairman 1994-2003, associated with drafting?
x: Kasturirangan drafted NEP 2020; the National Commission on Farmers report was Swaminathan's.

s: In which space shuttle mission was Kalpana Chawla killed on re-entry?
x: Kalpana Chawla of NASA died when Columbia (STS-107) broke up on re-entry.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anil Kakodkar — Atomic Energy Commission; Advanced Heavy Water Reactor
Tessy Thomas — ISRO; Aryabhata satellite team
U.R. Rao — DRDO; Agni-IV project director
Raja Ramanna — ISRO; drafting committee of NEP 2020
x: Anil Kakodkar was associated with the Atomic Energy Commission and the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor. Tessy Thomas was associated with DRDO, U.R. Rao with ISRO and Raja Ramanna with BARC.

s: With the development of which of the following is Anil Kakodkar associated?
x: Kakodkar (AEC) is linked with the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor and Pokhran-II; Agni-IV is Tessy Thomas's.

s: What was the code name of India's first nuclear test, Pokhran-I (1974), led by Raja Ramanna?
x: Pokhran-I (1974) was code-named 'Smiling Buddha'; Raja Ramanna led it.

s: With which field is Birbal Sahni associated?
x: Birbal Sahni is associated with palaeobotany; plant embryology is Maheshwari's, cereal rusts K.C. Mehta's and protein structure G.N. Ramachandran's field.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: C.N.R. Rao — Solid-state and structural chemistry
x: Jagdish Bhagwati is associated with economics, particularly trade, not palaeobotany. Palaeobotany is associated with Birbal Sahni.

s: What does the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis deal with?
o: Origin of life from simple chemicals
x: Oparin and Haldane independently proposed that life arose from simple chemicals in a reducing early atmosphere; cell theory was given by Schleiden and Schwann.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: R.H. Whittaker – Chromosomal theory of inheritance
x: Whittaker gave the five-kingdom classification; the chromosomal theory of inheritance is Sutton and Boveri's.

s: Who proposed the five-kingdom classification?
x: Whittaker proposed five kingdoms; Schleiden and Schwann gave cell theory and Sutton and Boveri the chromosomal theory.

s: With whom is the chromosomal theory of inheritance associated?
x: Sutton and Boveri gave the chromosomal theory of inheritance; Oparin-Haldane deals with the origin of life.

s: With which field is G.N. Ramachandran associated?
x: G.N. Ramachandran worked on protein structure; the Ramachandran plot is named after him.

s: With which field is P. Maheshwari associated?
x: P. Maheshwari is known for plant embryology; K.C. Mehta worked on cereal rusts.

s: Who proposed the cell theory?
x: Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory; Sutton and Boveri gave the chromosomal theory of inheritance.

s: With which field is K.C. Mehta associated?
x: K.C. Mehta worked on cereal rusts; P. Maheshwari on plant embryology.

s: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is associated with which of the following scientific discoveries?
o: Development of the first artificial satellite
Atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Structure of the DNA double helix
x: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is known for determining the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit, which provided insight into protein synthesis.

s: For which work did Har Gobind Khorana receive the Nobel Prize?
o: Determining the structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
Interpreting the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis
Discovering the structure of the neutron
x: Khorana was recognised for interpreting the genetic code and explaining its role in protein synthesis.

s: With whom did Venkatraman Ramakrishnan share the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009?
o: Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
x: The 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath for studies of the ribosome.

s: With whom did Har Gobind Khorana share the 1968 Nobel Prize?
o: Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
x: Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg.

s: During which period did Venkatraman Ramakrishnan serve as President of the Royal Society?
x: Ramakrishnan was President of the Royal Society from 2015 to 2020; he became FRS in 2003.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Khorana and Ramakrishnan?
o: Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968
Ramakrishnan received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009
Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009
Ramakrishnan studied the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
x: Khorana's Nobel was in Physiology or Medicine (1968); the 2009 Chemistry Nobel went to Ramakrishnan.

s: Which of the following was first made by Har Gobind Khorana?
x: Khorana made the first synthetic gene and read the genetic code.

s: In which year was Venkatraman Ramakrishnan awarded the Padma Vibhushan?
x: Ramakrishnan got the Padma Vibhushan in 2010, after his 2009 Chemistry Nobel; he was knighted in 2012.

s: Which body was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, known for high-yielding dwarf wheat and rice?
o: Scientific Advisory Council to the PM
x: Swaminathan chaired the National Commission on Farmers; the Scientific Advisory Council to the PM was headed by C.N.R. Rao.

s: In which year did M.S. Swaminathan receive the first World Food Prize?
x: M.S. Swaminathan received the first World Food Prize in 1987.

s: How was M.S. Swaminathan awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024?
o: during his lifetime for literary contributions
during his lifetime for work in space science
posthumously for his contribution to agriculture
posthumously for work in nuclear physics
x: M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his contribution to agriculture.

s: With whom did M.S. Swaminathan do his Green Revolution work on dwarf wheat and rice?
x: Swaminathan worked with Norman Borlaug; Holley and Nirenberg shared Khorana's Nobel and Steitz shared Ramakrishnan's.

s: What title did the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) give M.S. Swaminathan?
x: UNEP called M.S. Swaminathan the 'Father of Economic Ecology' (UPPSC 2007). He is the architect of India's Green Revolution. The Blue Revolution is fisheries and the White Revolution is milk (linked to Verghese Kurien), and 'Father of Green Chemistry' is not his title.

s: Which solid-state and materials chemist headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister?
x: C.N.R. Rao, the foremost solid-state and materials chemist, headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the PM.

s:
Consider the following statements about scientists honoured with the Bharat Ratna:
1. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam received it in 1997.
2. C.N.R. Rao received it in 2014.
3. M.S. Swaminathan received it in 2024 during his lifetime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are true; Swaminathan's 2024 Bharat Ratna was posthumous.

s: With which field is C.N.R. Rao mainly associated?
x: C.N.R. Rao is one of the foremost scientists in solid-state and materials chemistry, including structural chemistry.

s: Where was Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, winner of the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, born?
x: Ramakrishnan was born at Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu (asked in APPSC-GS 2012). Erode is Ramanujan's birthplace and Bhimavaram is Yellapragada SubbaRow's. Raipur is the birthplace of neither.

s: Yellapragada SubbaRow, associated with important contributions to biochemistry and medicine, was born at which place?
x: Yellapragada SubbaRow was born at Bhimavaram. Guntur district is associated with Yelavarthy Nayudamma.

s: The Fiske–SubbaRow method is associated with the study of the role of which substances in muscle?
x: Yellapragada SubbaRow contributed to understanding the role of ATP and phosphocreatine in muscle through the Fiske–SubbaRow method.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Yelavarthy Nayudamma?
o: He served as Director of the Central Leather Research Institute, Chennai
The Kanishka bombing in which he died occurred in 1986
He died in the bombing of Air India Flight 182 (Kanishka)
x: The Kanishka bombing in which Nayudamma died took place in 1985, not 1986.

s: Of which institution was Yelavarthy Nayudamma, born in Guntur, the director?
x: Nayudamma, the leather technologist, directed CLRI Chennai; he died in the Kanishka bombing (1985).

s: Which of the following drugs is associated with Yellapragada SubbaRow?
x: SubbaRow is linked with methotrexate, folic acid, aureomycin and Hetrazan.

s: Which of the following was synthesised by Yellapragada SubbaRow?
x: Yellapragada SubbaRow, born at Bhimavaram, worked on folic acid, methotrexate, aureomycin and Hetrazan.
